context_only: # tp v1.0.1 — tp says what round 1 will read

tasks.title: Export the uncut floor count from internal/engine
tasks.acceptance: internal/engine exports the uncut floor population as a function and internal/cli/ground.go's groundFloorSize calls it instead of duplicating the count, with lines_removed read on every edit. Verified by running on one fixture, a spec carrying cut units and no frontmatter: the exported function equals the line count of `tp ground <spec> --units` while the candidate-inclusive population does not. The closure states why neither engine.FloorUnits nor engine.FloorIndexRows was the answer, their difference being identically zero against real cut counts of 33, 15, 97, 53 and 6 across five specs, and says whether GroundCoverageOf's Emitted now calls the new function or stays separate.
tasks.closed_reason:
engine.FloorSize(rows []FloorIndexRow) int now exports the uncut floor population in internal/engine/floor.go -- it counts index rows carrying a hash, on 2.2's convention that the absence of the hash is the cut -- and internal/cli/ground.go's groundFloorSize is a one-line delegation to it, so the quantity has one definition serving both tp ground's floor_size and the lint field 2 specifies.
- Verified by running on one fixture, internal/cli's --units fixture (four candidate units, two cut by the arms, no frontmatter): tp ground spec.md --units prints 2 lines and engine.FloorSize returns 2, while the candidate-inclusive population is 4. TestFloorSizeIsTheUnitsListingsLineCount in internal/cli/ground_floor_size_test.go was written first and observed red twice -- once as undefined, then against a deliberate mutant body returning len(rows), which failed 4 against 2 and collapsed cut to 0, so the test discriminates the two populations instead of asserting a tautology. Re-measured on real specs, --units line count equals engine.FloorSize on spec/1.0.1.md (82), spec/0.37.0.md (173), spec/0.36.0.md (244) and spec/0.34.0.md (95).
- Neither engine.FloorUnits nor engine.FloorIndexRows was the answer: FloorUnits returns 2.1's candidate units with the arms' cuts included, and FloorIndexRows gives every candidate a row unconditionally because 2.2 announces the cut set, so their difference is identically zero. Re-derived here rather than inherited: the difference is 0 on all six specs measured (1.0.1, 0.37.0, 0.36.0, 0.35.0, 0.34.0, 0.31.1) whose real cut counts are 41, 53, 97, 100, 93 and 7.
- GroundCoverageOf's Emitted stays separate and does not call FloorSize. Emitted is the size of the emitted-id SET GroundCoverageOf must build anyway for its off-floor branch, and a set is not a row count: an index carrying one id twice would make FloorSize the larger of the two, and Dispositioned, which counts units, could then never reach it, breaking the bound Emitted's own doc states. The decision is recorded in FloorSize's doc comment so a later refactor does not collapse them.
- 2's table now names the derivation and the test in its last two columns, as 2 asks the implementing task to do, and its paragraph's claim that no exported function returns the uncut population is put in the past tense; review_panel's two columns stay task 4's. python3 scripts/check-spec-code-citations.py spec/1.0.1.md exits 0.
- Quality gate green: check-suite-state.sh 0, golangci-lint run 0, check-deadcode.sh 0, check-complexity.sh 0.

tasks.title: tp lint reports the two floor quantities
tasks.acceptance: `tp lint <spec>` emits floor_size and cut as siblings of structured_elements, with section 6 row 1's test and a cut test both written first and observed red against the unfixed code on one shared fixture, a spec with at least one cut unit and no frontmatter. A third test pins that lint's payload is byte-identical under --compact and --quiet, which is what section 2 claims and what round 2 measured. Section 2's derived by and pinned by cells for both fields are filled in with the real function and test names copied from the tests, and committed as part of this task.
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp lint emits floor_size and cut as siblings of structured_elements, both from engine.FloorSize over engine.FloorIndexRows(text, engine.FloorAnchorOf(text)) -- the one derivation tp ground reads, so no second definition of floor_size exists.
- All three tests were written first and observed RED against the unfixed code, failing on the absent key. After implementing, the mutant §6 row 1 names -- floorSize := len(floorRows) -- was applied and run: TestLintFloorSizeIsTheUnitsListingsLineCount failed 'expected 2, actual 4' and TestLintCutIsTheFloorIndexRowCountLessFloorSize failed 'expected 2, actual 0', the exact collapse §2 records. The mutant was reverted and the file verified byte-identical to its pre-mutant copy.
- The shared fixture is groundUnitsFixtureSpec: 4 candidate units, 2 cut, no frontmatter. Both halves of the precondition are asserted, not assumed -- require.False on a leading triple-dash and require.Greater(candidates, printed).
- Measured rather than copied: two six-line frontmatter blocks over that same fixture, one moved the --units listing from 2 units to 3 while the other moved nothing, so whether frontmatter separates the two commands depends on its content. Both comments say that instead of restating the spec's figure.
- TestLintPayloadIsByteIdenticalUnderCompactAndQuiet compares stdout BYTES under plain, --compact and --quiet; re-measured rather than trusting round 2's figure: 851 bytes on the fixture and 3408 on spec/1.0.1.md, identical md5 in all three forms.
- On spec/1.0.1.md: floor_size 83, cut 41, and tp ground spec/1.0.1.md --units prints 83 lines. Swept every spec/*.md and spec/backlog/*.md: lint's floor_size equals the --units line count on all of them, no exceptions.
- §2's cells now name the two lint tests. The cell filled in advance named TestFloorSizeIsTheUnitsListingsLineCount, which pins engine.FloorSize and never runs tp lint -- measured green under row 1's own mutant while both lint tests went red, so the cell was corrected rather than defended. The --compact/--quiet sentence names the third test. The spec still lints at 0 errors 0 warnings; a section-size warning the first draft introduced was removed by trimming the added prose.
- Gate green in four separately-run steps, each exit code read on its own: check-suite-state.sh 0, golangci-lint run 0 (0 issues), check-deadcode.sh 0, check-complexity.sh 0. runLint was already in scripts/baseline-funlen.txt, so no new or stale ratchet entry.

tasks.title: Split resolveRolePanel into resolver plus refusing wrapper
tasks.acceptance: resolveRolePanel becomes a pure resolution function plus a wrapper carrying the refusals and both output.Notice loops, and its two callers, internal/cli/review.go and internal/cli/audit.go, keep the wrapper with stdout, stderr and exit codes diffed identical before and after on the same tree, including the auditors-only refusal path. The task's first act is the decision section 7 asks for, since engine.roleUnits is already a pure resolution serving a read-only consumer: the closure says whether the shared pure half landed in internal/engine beside it or in internal/cli, and why a third copy was avoided. Tests are written red first and their names are then written into section 7, which currently says task 3 names them.
tasks.closed_reason:
The pure half landed in internal/engine as engine.ResolveRolePanel (internal/engine/rolepanel.go), not in internal/cli, and that was the task's first act. engine.roleUnits already held the same resolution for tp resume's read-only oracle, so a shared half in cli would have left that copy standing and made tp lint's the third — the shape §7 rejects. Putting it in engine instead reduced two copies to one: roleUnits now calls it, the cli wrapper calls it, and tp lint will be the third consumer of one resolution.
- The split: engine.ResolveRolePanel returns a RolePanel{Frontmatter, Roles, Disabled, Warnings} plus an error, and neither writes nor exits. internal/cli/resolveRolePanel keeps everything that refuses — the exit 3 abort on a malformed role file, the notice loop, refuseSpecCoverageDeactivated (auditors only) and refuseEmptyPhase — in §2.6's order. The cli rolePanel struct is unchanged, so review.go and audit.go are untouched by this commit series.
- Both callers diffed identical, not reasoned about. A 19-case command matrix over tp review and tp audit — both refusals, both notice loops in isolation and together (pinning their stderr order), the exit 3 malformed-role path in both phases, plain emission from a user corpus and from the embedded corpus, --role, --no-state and stateful runs, and the refusal-writes-nothing-to-disk check — was captured with a binary built at HEAD before the change and again after: stdout, stderr and exit code are byte-identical in all 19, including the auditors-only path (spec-coverage deactivated: exit 2 with the verbatim message, and the same when both refusals are armed, where spec-coverage still wins). tp resume was also diffed before/after on tp's own repo and on a review-phase fixture that exercises roleUnits: identical.
- The measurement §7 rests on was reproduced first, in a scratch fixture: on a corpus whose only reviewer declares domains: [prose] against a spec declaring domain: software, tp review writes exactly 86 bytes of notice to stderr and tp lint on the same tree writes none.
- Tests were written red first and the red was informative, not just a build error. After the compile failure I wrote the resolver as roleUnits' body promoted verbatim — the careless third-copy version — and watched two of the three engine tests fail for the reason expected: the corpus error came back nil and Warnings came back nil. Test 1 passed against that draft, which is recorded in §7: it does not stand alone.
- Three mutants were then built against the finished code and reverted: moving the notice loop into the resolver (engine test 3 fails on non-empty stderr; the cli test's review byte count goes 86 to 172), dropping refuseSpecCoverageDeactivated from the wrapper (the cli spec-coverage sub-test fails), and moving the empty-phase refusal into the resolver (engine test 1 does not fail — it kills the package test binary, which is the observable form of the defect).
- §7 now records the decision inline in its alternatives paragraph and replaces its 'Task 3 names them' placeholder with a table naming TestResolveRolePanel_ResolvesAnEmptiedPhaseWithoutRefusing, TestResolveRolePanel_ReturnsTheCorpusErrorInsteadOfExiting, TestResolveRolePanel_ReturnsWarningsWithoutWritingThem (internal/engine) and TestRolePanelWrapper_RefusalsAndNoticesStayOnTheWrapper (internal/cli), plus the three mutants and the honest note that row 1 does not discriminate alone.
- The two-caller claim was counted, not assumed: a search for resolveRolePanel across the repository returns its definition plus exactly two call sites, internal/cli/review.go:569 and internal/cli/audit.go:306.
- Quality gate, each step's exit code read separately: check-suite-state.sh 0, golangci-lint run 0 (0 issues), check-deadcode.sh 0, check-complexity.sh 0. Dogfooded with a freshly built /tmp/tp-dev/tp: tp lint spec/1.0.1.md exit 0 with 0 issues, tp resume exit 0.
Out of scope: tp lint does not call the resolver yet — the review_panel field and lint's empty-stderr guarantee are the next task's. The cli test pins lint's empty stderr today as a baseline, and the test comment says so rather than claiming it discriminates.

tasks.title: tp lint reports review_panel
tasks.acceptance: `tp lint <spec>` emits review_panel as a JSON list of reviewer role ids equal to those a round-1 `tp review <spec>` emission with no --diff-from carries, obtained through resolver-split's pure function so that lint gains no second derivation. Section 6 row 2 is written first and observed red on its constructed fixture, a temporary corpus in which exactly one role declares domains and a spec whose frontmatter does not match, reproducing the recorded counts of one role at HEAD against two under the mutant. No test asserts parity across this repository's own corpus, because no reviewer role in it declares domains and the filter is therefore inert, which round 2 measured as zero domain-mismatch skips over every spec.

tasks.title: Pin the sibling rule that still reports
tasks.acceptance: A test in internal/engine covers section 6 row 8 on the fixture that separates, a backticked section-and-step reference whose target section holds a numbered list shorter than the step named, giving broken-cross-ref one and vague-language zero at HEAD against broken-cross-ref zero under a mutant that blanks inline spans for every rule, with the mutant built and observed red before the test is accepted. The closure measures orphan-list-item's invariance under the same mutant rather than arguing it, which is the half of row 8's proof round 2 found unmeasured. Rows 4 through 7 close with --covered-by citing 65406160 and each existing test's actual counts, which differ from the rows' fixture counts and are quoted as they are.
source_sections: ## 3. The fence and the inline span

tasks.title: Ship the spec-writing rules to SKILL.md
tasks.acceptance: Every bullet in section 4 except the last, which is precedent, lands in skills/tp/SKILL.md, and the closure gives the count it derived from the bullet list rather than restating a number the spec does not carry. The fenced-command rule as shipped names both the interpreter and the binary, since naming bash alone leaves the binary free and round 2 recorded that gap. For each rule the closure states whether an author can check it while writing or only after a grading round, because a rule judgeable only afterwards costs rounds rather than saving them.

tasks.title: Document the three lint fields for release
tasks.acceptance: README.md documents the three fields tp lint adds, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json's version is bumped before any tag. The release notes state the case the cycle measured, that review_panel replaces an emission with a lint invocation, and cite spec/1.0.1-measurements.md section 11 for the byte counts rather than quoting them. They also say plainly that the release shipped with its review round unconverged at its cap, and why: five grading rounds refuted five successive sets of sentences about code that did not exist yet.

tasks.title: Pin what lint reports where review refuses
tasks.acceptance: When a spec deactivates every reviewer, `tp lint` reports review_panel as an empty JSON list and exits 0 while `tp review` still exits 2, each pinned by a test written first and observed red. Lint emits none of the wrapper's notices, measured as empty stderr on a corpus patched to make review write them, where round 2 measured review at 86 bytes against lint at zero. Section 6 row 3 is written on its fixture, a spec deactivating one role that is actually a reviewer in the corpus, reproducing the recorded counts of one role at HEAD against two under a mutant that ignores the frontmatter override.

tasks.title: REFERENCE.md distinguishes the two floor_size quantities
tasks.acceptance: skills/tp/REFERENCE.md states that lint's floor_size is the live text's floor while the floor_size in tp review's ungrounded envelope is the latest emitted round's frozen index, and gives the condition under which they agree. The paragraph is written after lint's field exists so that both quantities can be run and compared rather than described, and the closure quotes the two numbers it saw diverge on one spec.
